article.hook: You’re still fixing what’s already good enough. The South Node in Virgo rolls up sleeves for nearly two years, nudging us to stop polishing and start releasing. It’s less about perfecting and more about tolerating imperfection.
article.lived: For about eighteen months, we catch ourselves rereading emails to tweak grammar that doesn’t matter or double-checking steps in routines that already work. Meetings stretch longer because we want every detail right, yet solutions stall as we circle back to what’s already clear. You notice the urge to correct small errors in others, even when the bigger picture doesn’t need it. It’s a collective itch for precision that drags out the process instead of speeding it up.
article.turn: When the drive to fix overwhelms, it traps us in endless revisions and second-guessing. Obsessing over tiny flaws lets everything else slide, turning competence into paralysis. You can’t improve what’s already done well just by staring at it longer. Let some cracks show or you’ll never move forward.
